task_name: Delete attachments and clean up soft-deleted cards

concerns_addressed: The cycle-1 cover-reassignment gap is resolved: the public DELETE test removes cover A while attachment B remains, fetches the public card response, and asserts B is the sole remaining ordered attachment before deleting B and asserting the empty state (server/src/routes/card-attachments-delete.integration.test.ts:125-185).

The original non-cover deletion scenario remains additive and still verifies 204 responses, row and file removal, stable cards.version, attachment_removed activity with a current column, attachment.removed SSE, and final empty hydration (server/src/routes/card-attachments-delete.integration.test.ts:30-123).

DELETE remains behind the shared ownership-chain guard; the transaction additionally scopes the active card and attachment to the workspace/card before deleting (server/src/routes/card-attachments.ts:38-45, 51-83).

Attachment rows are deleted before post-commit best-effort cleanup, and cleanup rejection is contained with Promise.allSettled (server/src/routes/card-attachments.ts:85-145; server/src/routes/card-attachment-cleanup.ts:6-18).

Soft-delete explicitly selects and deletes attachment rows while the card is locked, preserves the existing delete activity and card-deleted events, leaves cards.version unchanged, and performs file cleanup after commit without touching tracker tables (server/src/routes/cards.ts:650-719; server/src/routes/card-attachments-soft-delete.integration.test.ts:29-99).

strengths: The new cover test exercises the real public HTTP DELETE and GET endpoints in the required A-then-B order; the response containing only B proves deterministic cover reassignment through response hydration (server/src/routes/card-attachments-delete.integration.test.ts:138-159).

The implementation keeps the transaction boundary clear: card locking and ownership checks precede attachment row deletion, activity recording is transactional, and file cleanup plus realtime publication occur only after commit (server/src/routes/card-attachments.ts:51-145).

Best-effort cleanup is isolated in a reusable helper and cannot convert a committed deletion into a failed request; the soft-delete test covers a simulated unlink failure and verifies the card remains soft-deleted with rows removed (server/src/routes/card-attachment-cleanup.ts:6-18; server/src/routes/card-attachments-soft-delete.integration.test.ts:51-85).

Existing card history/event behavior and optimistic-locking/tracker isolation are preserved and explicitly asserted; no hard card deletion or card-event deletion was introduced (server/src/routes/cards.ts:650-719; server/src/routes/card-attachments-soft-delete.integration.test.ts:71-99).
The cycle-2 change is limited to the T7-owned test coverage, with the original scenarios retained; focused attachment tests, card mutation tests, typecheck, and Biome checks were reported green.
